Greene Says Both Parties Backed Ukraine War Funding
Greene took to
X
to reiterate her opposition to funding Ukraine’s war effort, saying she had warned from the start about its potential consequences.
"I also said from day 1 that it would be bad for specific industries like grain and fertilizer and energy," Greene wrote, criticizing Republicans and Democrats for voting to fund the war.
She also renewed her demand for an audit of the spending, saying, "And I never got the audit I demanded that passed."
Obvious from the beginning, which is why I never voted to fund the Ukraine war.
I also said from day 1 that it would be bad for specific industries like grain and fertilizer and energy.
Yet both R’s and D’s voted to fund it.
And I never got the audit I demanded that passed.

Greene was responding to Musk’s post arguing that Ukraine’s political and business elites had benefited financially from the hundreds of billions of dollars directed toward the country, while ordinary Ukrainians faced conscription and battlefield deaths.

In a follow-up post, Musk alleged that some U.S. taxpayer money eventually returns to the country through intermediaries to finance political campaigns, claiming this helps explain why some politicians prioritize Ukraine over domestic concerns.
Ukraine Says Starlink Restrictions Still Disrupt Military Operations
Musk’s comments came amid an ongoing dispute over SpaceX’s Starlink and military-focused
Starshield
satellite communications systems, which Ukraine relies on for military connectivity and drone operations.
Ukrainian officials have said restrictions introduced since Oct. 14 have affected drones traveling faster than 100 mph, disrupting some missions targeting Russian military logistics.
Despite President
Donald Trump’s
statements suggesting the
, Ukrainian officials said Friday that the restrictions remained in place.
"Every day matters for Ukraine, because every Ukrainian life matters," Ukraine’s Deputy Ambassador to the U.S. D
enys Sienik
wrote on X, adding that officials were still waiting for the restrictions to be lifted.

Starshield/Starlink speed restrictions remain in place. Every day matters for Ukraine, because every Ukrainian life matters. Our people are waiting for positive news, hoping that the restrictions will be lifted and our defenders will have the capabilities they need to protect…
President
Volodymyr Zelenskyy
also said the speed limits remained in place.

The speed limits on Starlink and Starshield are still there. The speed has not been restored. And the delivery of interceptors to protect us against Russian ballistic missiles is still delayed. We’re waiting for interceptors that were already agreed on. But they are still not…
Dmitri Alperovitch
, chairman of the
Silverado Policy Accelerator
, told CNBC that Ukrainian forces were losing drones and facing limitations in striking Russian logistics.
Lawmakers Push for Reliable Satellite Communications
The dispute has prompted bipartisan lawmakers to urge Defense Secretary
Pete Hegseth
to expand Starshield arrangements and ensure uninterrupted communications support for Ukraine.
Meanwhile, Ukraine is exploring alternatives. Its Defense Ministry signed a letter of intent with
Nokia
and Finnish satellite intelligence company
ICEYE
to explore sovereign satellite communications capabilities, the report noted.
